entities.name: Bonino da Campione
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bonino da Campione, a preeminent Italian sculptor active between approximately 1350 and 1390, stands as a pivotal figure in the development of Late Gothic art in Northern Italy. Hailing from the renowned Campionesi workshop tradition, a family of master stonemasons and sculptors from Campione d'Italia, Bonino elevated the Lombard Gothic style with his distinctive blend of naturalism, pathos, and monumental scale. His career was largely shaped by the patronage of powerful regional lords, most notably the Della Scala family of Verona, for whom he executed some of his most significant commissions, leaving an indelible mark on funerary sculpture of the era.

Bonino's core achievements are epitomized by the elaborate monumental tombs he crafted for the Della Scala dynasty in Verona. His masterpiece, the Arca di Cansignorio della Scala (completed c. 1375-1376) at Santa Maria Antica, showcases his virtuosity: a towering, multi-tiered structure adorned with equestrian statues, allegorical figures, and intricate reliefs depicting scenes from the life of the deceased. Similarly, the Arca di Mastino II della Scala (c. 1371) demonstrates his capacity to imbue traditional Gothic forms with a new emotional intensity and sculptural complexity, moving beyond earlier, more static effigies. These works established a standard for funerary monuments, integrating architecture and sculpture to create profound statements of power and piety.
